title: Use of pepper spray questioned after man's death
article: Questions are once again being raised about the use of pepper spray, after a Regina man died Tuesday evening.
Vernon Dale Crowe, 21, had a seizure, and was being treated by ambulance staff. When he became combative, police were called. After being assaulted, an officer used pepper spray to subdue the man.
"I wouldn't say [pepper spray] is used all the time, but it is not uncommon for us to use pepper spray," says Regina's police chief, Cal Johnston
"If the person is threatening or has already become assaultive to the officer or other people, perhaps at that point, pepper spray would be used," he explains.
Johnston says pepper spray is not fatal in itself. But he says there have been cases where it contributed to deaths in people with other medical problems.
The whole ordeal was played out on the street outside the Souls Harbor Mission, a soup kitchen and drop-in centre for Regina's poor.
The mission's founder, Gerri Carroll, says she had known Crowe for 11 years, and had never experienced any problem with him.
"He was a very kind person. He was very easy to talk to. He had a compassion for people that were here," Carroll added.
It is still not clear if the pepper spray had anything to do with the man's death. Autopsy results have not been released yet.
